QuestionStmt.S: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & -\sin \theta \\ \sin \theta & \cos \theta \end{bmatrix}$, then the matrix $A^{-3}$ when $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}$ is equal to

Solution.S:
Step 1: The matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{bmatrix}$ is a rotation matrix.

Step 2: For a rotation matrix, $A^n = \begin{bmatrix} \cos n\theta & -\sin n\theta \\ \sin n\theta & \cos n\theta \end{bmatrix}$.

Step 3: Therefore, $A^{-3} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos(-3\theta) & -\sin(-3\theta) \\ \sin(-3\theta) & \cos(-3\theta) \end{bmatrix}$.

Step 4: Given $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}$, we have $-3\theta = -\frac{\pi}{2}$.

Step 5: Now, $\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0$ and $\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -1$.

Step 6: So, $A^{-3} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -(-1) \\ -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}}$$

Hence, the correct option is A.
